minority stream to an alternative route entirely. Interleaving two streams through one space is almost always worse than sending one of them somewhere else. 4. Identify why the opposing stream exists. People rarely walk against a crowd with

diagnostic sign is people making progress in two opposite directions along the same axis, not merely people looking disordered. A jammed crowd also looks chaotic while going nowhere, and it requires the opposite response, so the two must be

Gate and Chokepoint Bottleneck Standard Operating Procedure Scope. Applies to entries, exits, turnstiles, stairways, bridges, tunnels, ramps and any constriction where the walkway narrows and arrival rate can exceed discharge rate. Recognit

advisory.situation: NORMAL at 15s in Approach. 32 people tracked; peak local density 0.47 persons/m2; mean speed 1.68 m/s; crowd pressure 0.321 s^-2. Fused risk 0.36 (moderate). Over the last 15s: density 0.0 to 0.5 persons/m2 (+11177%); mean speed 0.00 to 1.68 m/s; occupancy 1 to 32 (+31).
advisory.mechanism: High directional disorder: the vector sum of velocities collapses relative to the scalar sum, so people move but the crowd does not.
advisory.root_cause: Counter-Flow Conflict detected at confidence 0.22. Measured evidence: two opposing movement axes detected (counter-flow index 0.30) with the crowd still moving at 1.68 m/s.
actions: MARSHALS: impose one-way movement through Approach and physically separate the two streams with line barriers. Assemble at Approach edge.
CONTROL: divert the minority stream rather than trying to interleave them. Divert to Discharge.
PA: announce the one-way direction before density rises -- this is cheap now and impossible later.
advisory.broadcast: Approach is now one-way only. If you are heading the other way, please use Discharge.
advisory.time_budget: On the current trend, CRITICAL is reached in about 17s. WARNING: the recommended action needs about 180s to take effect, which is 163s LONGER than the time available. Escalate one level immediately and act on the faster intervention.
